\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{લોન} (lon)}{લોન (lon)}]{\gu{લોન} (lon) — a bank loan}

\label{lesson:GU-C425-lon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a token, then the Gujarati for a bank card.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{લોન}}
\textbf{\gu{લોન}} — \emph{lon} — \textquotedblleft{}a bank loan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{તેણે} \gu{ઘર} \gu{માટે} \gu{બેંકમાંથી} \gu{લોન} \gu{લીધી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{teṇe ghar māṭe beṅkmā̃thī lon līdhī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He took a loan from the bank for a house.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{લોન}} (\emph{lon}) is borrowed from English \emph{loan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lon}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lon}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{teṇe ghar māṭe beṅkmā̃thī lon līdhī.} — He took a loan from the bank for a house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a token, then the Gujarati for a bank card, then say \emph{lon} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{હપતો} (hapto)}{હપતો (hapto)}]{\gu{હપતો} (hapto) — an instalment}

\label{lesson:GU-C425-hapto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a bank card, then the Gujarati for a bank loan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{હપતો}}
\textbf{\gu{હપતો}} — \emph{hapto} — \textquotedblleft{}an instalment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મારે} \gu{લોનનો} \gu{હપતો} \gu{દસમી} \gu{તારીખે} \gu{ભરવો} \gu{પડે} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māre lonno hapto dasmī tārīkhe bharvo paḍe che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I have to pay the loan instalment on the tenth.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{હપતો}} (\emph{hapto}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{hafta}, \textquotedblleft{}a week\textquotedblright{}: a sum paid at regular times, once by the week, now often by the month.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{દલાલ} (dalāl)}{દલાલ (dalāl)}]{\gu{દલાલ} (dalāl) — a broker; a middleman}

\label{lesson:GU-C425-dalal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a bank loan, then the Gujarati for an instalment.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{દલાલ}}
\textbf{\gu{દલાલ}} — \emph{dalāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a broker; a middleman\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{દલાલે} \gu{અમને} \gu{સસ્તો} \gu{ફ્લેટ} \gu{બતાવ્યો}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dalāle amne sasto phleṭ batāvyo.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The broker showed us a cheap flat.

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{દલાલ}} (\emph{dalāl}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{dallāl}, \textquotedblleft{}one who shows the way; a broker\textquotedblright{}, which came through Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ગીરો} (gīro)}{ગીરો (gīro)}]{\gu{ગીરો} (gīro) — a pledge; a pawn (left as security)}

\label{lesson:GU-C425-giro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for an instalment, then the Gujarati for a broker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ગીરો}}
\textbf{\gu{ગીરો}} — \emph{gīro} — \textquotedblleft{}a pledge; a pawn (left as security)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{તેણે} \gu{ઘરેણાં} \gu{ગીરો} \gu{મૂક્યાં}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{teṇe ghareṇā̃ gīro mūkyā̃.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She pawned her jewellery.
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ગીરો}} (\emph{gīro}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{giraw}, \textquotedblleft{}a pledge, a pawn\textquotedblright{}: what you leave with a lender until you pay.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ચૂકતે} (cūkte)}{ચૂકતે (cūkte)}]{\gu{ચૂકતે} (cūkte) — paid in full; settled}

\label{lesson:GU-C425-cukte}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a broker, then the Gujarati for a pledge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ચૂકતે}}
\textbf{\gu{ચૂકતે}} — \emph{cūkte} — \textquotedblleft{}paid in full; settled\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{આજે} \gu{મેં} \gu{લોન} \gu{ચૂકતે} \gu{કરી}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{āje mẽ lon cūkte karī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Today I paid off the loan in full.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ચૂકતે}} (\emph{cūkte}) is built on the same stem as \gu{ચૂકવવું}, to pay off, which goes back to \emph{*cukk}, \textquotedblleft{}to fall short, to stop\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 4848).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cūkte}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āje mẽ lon cūkte karī.} — Today I paid off the loan in full.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a broker, then the Gujarati for a pledge, then say \emph{cūkte} again
\end{itemize}
